correctness.rationale: The Baronti--Bertella definition and symmetry of the pointwise quantity are taken from the inspected primary full text. The new proof fixes one hexagon edge by dihedral symmetry, exhaustively classifies all solutions of \(N(x+y)=N(x-y)\) into eight exact line segments, and maps those segments to two canonical one-parameter families. For \(\lambda\ge1\), each family has an explicit crossing of two lower-bounding facet values; derivative signs force the minimum to that crossing. The minus family yields the sharp bound \(N(x+\lambda y)^2/(1+\lambda^2)\ge32/45\), and the explicit pair \(x=(1,1/3)\), \(y=(-1/3,-1)\), \(\lambda=3\) attains equality.
risks: The proof relies on an exact finite active-facet classification; the checker certifies all cases and the public proof explains the continuum reduction.
No finite sampling is used for the global inequality.

value.rationale: The finding gives a sharp exact value of a recently introduced standard geometric constant on the canonical affine-regular hexagonal plane, a basic nonsmooth non-Hilbert benchmark. It is not a routine substitution: the value comes from a complete classification of unit isosceles pairs and an interior scale \(\lambda=3\), showing geometry that is invisible in the universal bounds. The facet-classification method is reusable for other polyhedral \(H_p\) calculations.
risks: The contribution is a canonical exact benchmark rather than a full \(p\)-profile or all-polygon classification.
